steps: Here the main agent will assess risk in a contracts folder using two subagents, a researcher and an analyst. That works because its allowed tools include the Agent tool.
First, the main agent delegates the opening task, finding renewal dates, to the researcher through the Agent tool.
The researcher works in a fresh, isolated context, with no parent history. It greps the folder for renewal date with its own read tools and finds three files with three dates.
Now only its final message returns as the tool result, three dates. The grep calls stay behind. The memo comes back, not the notebook, so the main context stays clean.
Next comes the analyst. It also starts with a fresh context and cannot see the parent's history, so the brief it receives must carry all the context it needs.
So the parent pastes the three findings into the brief, and the analyst rates them: two high risk and one low. The brief is all it sees.
Finally, the parent merges the two memos into one complete assessment, in two turns, for about six tenths of a cent.
